text: Adopted Herbert Simon's bounded rationality as the seminar's decision-making frame; satisficing under cognitive and information constraints replaces the classical utility-maximiser idealisation in every case study.

queries.text: which framing replaced classical utility-maximisation in the seminar and who proposed it
simon bounded rationality satisficing utility maximiser decision frame

text: Allen Newell's Unified Theories of Cognition landed in 1990 and argued that a single cognitive architecture should reproduce the full range of intelligent behaviour rather than a single paradigm task.

queries.text: which 1990 monograph argued a single architecture should explain the full span of cognition
newell unified theories cognition 1990 architecture paradigm

text: SOAR, designed by Newell, Laird, and Rosenbloom, treats problem-solving as search in problem spaces with chunking as the sole learning mechanism; production rules fire against a working memory each decision cycle.

queries.text: how does the SOAR architecture organise problem-solving and which single mechanism handles learning
soar newell laird rosenbloom chunking problem space production rule

text: GOMS, the Goals-Operators-Methods-Selection-rules model from Card, Moran, and Newell, gives an engineering-grade estimator for expert task time in human-computer interaction without running a user study.

queries.text: which HCI estimator predicts expert task time without running a user study and who devised it
goms card moran newell goal operator method selection hci

text: John Anderson's ACT-R integrates a symbolic production system with subsymbolic activation dynamics; declarative chunks decay and reactivate probabilistically, so the architecture fits neural timing data and rule-based behaviour in one model.

queries.text: how does ACT-R combine symbolic rules with subsymbolic dynamics and whose framework is it
act-r anderson production chunk activation subsymbolic decay

text: David Marr's Vision, published posthumously in 1982, recast visual perception as an information-processing problem solved through a sequence of representations from primal sketch to 3D model.

queries.text: which 1982 posthumous book framed perception as an information-processing pipeline of representations
marr vision 1982 primal sketch 3d model representation pipeline

text: Marr's three levels of analysis separate the computational, algorithmic, and implementational; the seminar insists every theory specify which level it lives at before arguing about its empirical adequacy.

queries.text: which tri-level scheme does the seminar require every theory to locate itself in
marr three levels computational algorithmic implementation analysis

text: Jerry Fodor's The Language of Thought argued that cognition operates over a combinatorial mental code called Mentalese; productivity and systematicity of thought are the core arguments, recycled later against connectionism.

queries.text: which Fodor monograph posited a combinatorial mental code and what arguments support it
fodor language thought mentalese productivity systematicity combinatorial

text: Fodor's Modularity of Mind hypothesises domain-specific, informationally encapsulated input systems separate from a holistic central cognition; the face-processing module is the canonical example in the perception chapter.

queries.text: which Fodor book partitions mind into encapsulated input modules and a holistic central system
fodor modularity mind informationally encapsulated input central

text: The faculty lounge's kettle lost its whistle gasket on Tuesday and a handwritten sign now demands anyone brewing tea use the spare in the mug cupboard.

Daniel Dennett's intentional stance treats ascribing beliefs and desires as a predictive strategy that works whenever the target behaves rationally; the stance is orthogonal to whether any literal inner representation exists.

queries.text: which Dennett framework treats belief-desire ascription as a predictive strategy rather than literal description
dennett intentional stance belief desire predictive rational strategy

text: Consciousness Explained by Dennett, 1991, develops the Multiple Drafts model against the Cartesian Theatre; there is no single place in the brain where conscious content becomes definite.

queries.text: which Dennett book proposed Multiple Drafts against the Cartesian Theatre picture of consciousness
dennett consciousness explained multiple drafts cartesian theatre 1991

text: Noam Chomsky's universal grammar posits an innate language faculty whose principles underlie every natural language; cross-linguistic parameter setting accounts for observed variation.

queries.text: whose theory posits an innate grammar whose parameters fix cross-linguistic variation
chomsky universal grammar innate language faculty parameter setting

text: The poverty-of-stimulus argument claims children acquire grammatical competence their input underdetermines, so some linguistic structure must be innately specified; the auxiliary-inversion case is the textbook illustration.

queries.text: which argument infers innate linguistic structure from the gap between input and acquired competence
poverty stimulus grammatical competence auxiliary inversion innate

text: Steven Pinker's The Language Instinct, 1994, popularised the nativist case by framing language as a biologically-evolved instinct; the book packages Chomskyan arguments for a general audience.

queries.text: which 1994 Pinker book packaged the nativist case about language for a general audience
pinker language instinct 1994 nativist chomsky popular evolved

text: Pinker's How the Mind Works extends an evolutionary-psychology reading of cognition across vision, language, and emotion; the seminar uses its mental-imagery chapter as a counterweight to pure connectionist accounts.

queries.text: which Pinker book pushes an evolutionary-psychology reading across vision, language, and emotion
pinker how mind works evolutionary psychology imagery connectionist

text: George Lakoff and Mark Johnson's Metaphors We Live By argues everyday cognition is structured by conceptual metaphor grounded in sensorimotor experience; the container and journey metaphors recur throughout.

queries.text: which Lakoff and Johnson book grounds cognition in sensorimotor-rooted conceptual metaphor
lakoff johnson metaphors we live by conceptual sensorimotor container

text: Andy Clark's extended mind thesis, co-written with David Chalmers, argues that notebooks and tools can constitute part of a cognitive system when they are reliably coupled to the agent's reasoning.

queries.text: whose thesis treats reliably-coupled external tools as parts of a cognitive system
clark chalmers extended mind notebook tool cognitive coupling

text: The seminar's embodied cognition stance rejects the view that thinking is abstract symbol manipulation and locates meaning in bodily and environmental interaction; it interrogates purely computational accounts throughout.

queries.text: which theoretical stance rejects abstract symbol manipulation in favour of bodily-environmental coupling
embodied cognition symbol manipulation body environment interaction

text: Joshua Tenenbaum's lab frames cognition as approximate Bayesian inference over structured generative models; the number-game experiment is the seminar's introduction to hierarchical priors in concept learning.

queries.text: whose lab frames cognition as Bayesian inference over generative models and which experiment anchors it
tenenbaum bayesian generative number game hierarchical prior concept

text: Thomas Griffiths and colleagues showed that rational analyses of memory, categorisation, and causal learning converge on Bayesian posteriors under reasonable priors; the tutorial chapter is assigned in week six.

queries.text: whose rational analyses show memory, categorisation, and causal learning reduce to Bayesian posteriors
griffiths rational analysis memory categorisation causal bayesian

text: Noah Goodman's probabilistic programming framework treats concepts as stochastic generative programs; the Church language and its successor WebPPL make the inferences first-class objects students can run in a browser.

queries.text: whose probabilistic-programming stack treats concepts as generative programs and which languages implement it
goodman probabilistic programming church webppl stochastic generative

text: The Rumelhart-McClelland PDP volumes of 1986 launched connectionism as a cognitive paradigm; distributed representations and backprop-trained multilayer networks replaced the pure symbolic account in perception modules.

queries.text: which 1986 two-volume set launched connectionism and displaced pure symbolic accounts in perception
rumelhart mcclelland pdp 1986 connectionism distributed backprop symbol

text: The past-tense learning model by Rumelhart and McClelland showed a single network producing regular and irregular inflections without explicit rules; Pinker and Prince's rebuttal became the canonical Words-and-Rules counter.

queries.text: which connectionist model drew a rule-free account of past tense and which symbolic rebuttal countered it
past tense rumelhart mcclelland pinker prince words rules connectionist

text: Karl Friston's free energy principle claims self-organising systems minimise variational free energy, which is equivalent to minimising prediction error in a generative model of their world.

queries.text: which Friston principle ties self-organisation to variational free-energy minimisation and prediction error
friston free energy variational prediction error generative self organise

text: The unit on predictive processing reframes perception, attention, and action as hierarchical Bayesian inference where top-down predictions meet bottom-up sensory prediction errors; Andy Clark's Surfing Uncertainty is the assigned primer.

queries.text: which framework casts perception and action as hierarchical Bayesian inference and which Clark book primers it
predictive processing hierarchical bayesian prediction error clark surfing

text: Bernard Baars' Global Workspace Theory posits a capacity-limited broadcast system that makes selected contents globally available to otherwise modular consumers; consciousness corresponds to workspace access.

queries.text: which Baars theory models consciousness as capacity-limited broadcast to otherwise modular consumers
baars global workspace broadcast modular consciousness capacity

text: Stanislas Dehaene's neuronal workspace extends Baars into a neurally-realised account: long-range pyramidal neurons in parietal and prefrontal cortex ignite when a stimulus crosses the access threshold.

queries.text: whose neuronal workspace extends Baars into a neurally-grounded ignition account
dehaene neuronal workspace baars ignition prefrontal parietal pyramidal

text: Giulio Tononi's Integrated Information Theory formalises consciousness as phi, the integrated information generated by a system above and beyond its parts; the axiomatic derivation is the week-eleven reading.

queries.text: whose theory quantifies consciousness as phi, the information integrated above and beyond parts
tononi iit integrated information phi axiomatic consciousness

text: IIT and Global Workspace Theory give incompatible verdicts on split-brain and cerebellum cases; the seminar tables these as the primary empirical arbiters between broadcast and integration accounts.

queries.text: which empirical cases pit IIT against Global Workspace Theory as arbiters of consciousness theories
iit global workspace split brain cerebellum arbiter consciousness

text: David Rosenthal's Higher-Order Thought theory requires a mental state to be the object of a thought about it to count as conscious; first-order representation alone is not sufficient.

queries.text: which Rosenthal theory demands a second-order thought for a state to be conscious
rosenthal higher order thought first order representation conscious

text: The mismatch-case objection to HOT concerns hallucinated higher-order thoughts without a matching first-order state; proponents bite the bullet and call the mismatch itself sufficient for phenomenal character.

queries.text: which objection to HOT exploits cases of higher-order thoughts without matching first-order states
hot mismatch case first order phenomenal bite bullet objection

text: Michael Graziano's attention schema theory treats subjective awareness as the brain's simplified internal model of its own attention; the model's accuracy is less important than its utility for social prediction.

queries.text: whose theory models awareness as the brain's internal model of its own attention
graziano attention schema model awareness social prediction

text: Daniel Kahneman's dual-systems account distinguishes fast intuitive System 1 from slow deliberate System 2; the cognitive-reflection test is the seminar's introductory diagnostic for switching between them.

queries.text: whose dual-systems account contrasts fast System 1 with slow System 2 and which test diagnoses switching
kahneman dual systems system 1 system 2 cognitive reflection test

text: Keith Stanovich refined dual-systems by distinguishing autonomous Type 1 from reflective Type 2 within a tripartite mind that includes an algorithmic level; rationality failures emerge when the reflective mind fails to override.

queries.text: whose tripartite-mind refinement of dual-systems distinguishes autonomous Type 1 from reflective Type 2
stanovich tripartite mind type 1 type 2 reflective override rationality

text: Francisco Varela, Evan Thompson, and Eleanor Rosch's The Embodied Mind, 1991, introduced enactivism: cognition is sense-making through the dynamic coupling of a living agent with its environment.

queries.text: which 1991 Varela Thompson Rosch book introduced enactivism as sense-making through agent-environment coupling
varela thompson rosch embodied mind 1991 enactivism sense making

text: Evan Thompson's Mind in Life extends enactivism with an autopoiesis-based biology of cognition; the seminar pairs its chapter three with Maturana and Varela for the life-mind continuity thesis.

queries.text: which Thompson book extends enactivism into autopoietic biology and underpins life-mind continuity
thompson mind life enactivism autopoiesis maturana life mind continuity

text: The 4E cognition umbrella bundles embodied, embedded, extended, and enactive approaches; the seminar uses 4E as a label for positions that share a rejection of purely internalist computational cognition.

queries.text: which umbrella term covers embodied, embedded, extended, and enactive cognition against internalist computational views
4e cognition embodied embedded extended enactive internalist

text: Preferred The Language Instinct over How the Mind Works for the intro reading; students land on the nativist argument faster without the evolutionary-psychology scaffolding first.

queries.text: which Pinker title does the seminar open with and why over its companion volume
pinker language instinct how mind works nativist evolutionary intro

text: Preferred ACT-R over SOAR for the modelling-lab track; its subsymbolic activation layer fits reaction-time data tighter without a second-pass calibration.

queries.text: which architecture does the modelling-lab track prefer over SOAR and on which empirical grounds
act-r soar subsymbolic reaction time modelling lab preference

text: Preferred Marr's tri-level frame over Chomsky's competence-performance split for the analytic scaffolding; it generalises outside linguistics without forcing a competence idealisation first.

queries.text: which analytic scaffolding does the seminar prefer to the competence-performance split and why
marr tri level chomsky competence performance scaffolding

text: The binding problem asks how distributed feature detectors yield unified percepts; temporal-synchrony, attention-based, and predictive-coding solutions remain unresolved across the cognitive-neuroscience literature.

queries.text: which unresolved puzzle asks how distributed features cohere into unified percepts across neuroscience
binding problem temporal synchrony attention predictive coding feature

text: Somebody left a half-finished crossword on the reading-room table and a pencilled note claiming 14-down is probably wrong.
Preferred predictive processing over classical sensorimotor accounts for the action chapter; the top-down prediction machinery handles motor control and perception with one inference scheme.

queries.text: which framework does the action chapter prefer over sensorimotor accounts for unifying motor and perception
predictive processing sensorimotor motor control inference unified

text: Jerry Fodor and Zenon Pylyshyn's 1988 critique of connectionism argued that distributed networks lack the systematicity and productivity a theory of thought needs; Smolensky's tensor-product binding is the assigned reply.

queries.text: which 1988 paper attacked connectionism on systematicity grounds and which reply gets assigned against it
fodor pylyshyn 1988 connectionism systematicity smolensky tensor

text: The Chinese Room argument by John Searle contends that syntactic symbol manipulation alone cannot constitute understanding; Dennett's systems reply and Churchland's luminous-room parody are paired readings.

queries.text: which Searle argument denies syntactic symbol manipulation yields understanding and which replies are paired
searle chinese room syntax understanding dennett churchland luminous

text: The hard problem of consciousness, framed by David Chalmers in 1995, separates the easy problems of cognitive function from why experience accompanies any of it; it anchors the terminology for the final unit.

queries.text: which Chalmers distinction separates the easy problems of cognition from the hard problem of experience
chalmers hard problem consciousness 1995 easy experience

text: Endel Tulving's episodic-semantic distinction and Baddeley and Hitch's working-memory model anchor the memory unit; the central executive coordinates the phonological loop and visuospatial sketchpad in the 1974 framing.

queries.text: which two frameworks anchor the memory unit and how does the 1974 working-memory model decompose
tulving episodic semantic baddeley hitch working memory executive loop

text: After the 2015 wave of failed social-priming replications, the seminar adopted a rule re-weighting cognitive-science findings by pre-registration status and effect-size stability before citing any result.

queries.text: which policy did the seminar adopt after 2015 social-priming failures for weighing cognitive-science findings
social priming pre registration 2015 effect size weight cognitive

text: Ran into a scope clash between IIT and predictive processing in the consciousness unit: IIT scores systems in the absence of input, while predictive processing requires a generative model driven by sensory evidence.

queries.text: which scope clash pits IIT against predictive processing on whether inputs are required to score consciousness
iit predictive processing scope generative sensory evidence clash
